The correlation between $AAPL and the Nasdaq 100 has now remained negative for 2 consecutive months.

This comes as $AAPL has gained +9.7% over this period, while the Nasdaq 100 has increased just +0.2%.

By comparison, in June 2025, the 3-month correlation stood at +0.90, as Apple and other technology stocks rallied together.

To put this into perspective, from 2006 through 2025, the correlation never fell below +0.30.

The divergence between Apple and the rest of the tech sector is unprecedented.

text: I don’t disagree with anything you say except your implicit view that there is no autonomous competition.  This is the same delusional thinking among $TSLA bulls from 2020-2021 when they insisted no one would be able to compete with TSLA in EV manufactured cost or scale, but wound up being sorely wrong in 2023-2025 as others (especially Chinese manufacturers) caught up to TSLA on manufactured cost.   The same is true now:  Waymo, BIDU, http://Pony.ai and others working with NVDA will be able to compete with TSLA in unsupervised autonomy, which will pressure TSLA’s current irrational 2026 P/E of 220x vs +45% long-term EPS growth.
